findings.evidence: stack-policy.md:151-154; stack-policy.yml now always passes --state-in/--state-out for full apply batches and coalesces into 'no-stack-automatic-batch'.
findings.fix: Remove the legacy-caller paragraph and state the guarantees as properties of stack-policy.yml.
findings.issue: Rollout narrative copied without adaptation: 'The batching guarantees below require a caller using checkpoint mode... Legacy per-event callers still use focused checks...; upgrading the checker alone does not change workflow scheduling.' This repo's caller already batches, so the text describes a transition state, not the policy.

findings.evidence: stack-policy.md:226-227 and :278; the workflow's concurrency group already implements global coalescing.
findings.fix: Drop the rollout clause (say focused --pr runs are uncheckpointed), and rewrite line 278 as a description of what stack-policy.yml does.
findings.issue: 'Without checkpoint arguments, the focused/backlog interface continues to support the deployed caller during rollout.' This is process/rollout status, and nothing will update it after rollout. Line 278 ('Automatic wakes can then coalesce globally') has the same problem: it is caller-design advice copied from the Tools docs, when this workflow already does it.

findings.evidence: stack-policy.md:285-288; the in-repo tests are scripts/test_stack_policy.py and scripts/test_stack_checkpoint_restore.py.
findings.fix: Link the TauCetiTools test file at the pinned revision 980a7a0e, or remove the paragraph and rely on the in-repo test commands already listed.
findings.issue: 'For local regression tests in TauCetiTools run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_stack_batch.py' gives a command for another repository with no path or link; run here, it fails because this repo has no tests/ directory.

summary: The new policy docs match the workflow's batching, restore and retention behaviour, but parts of stack-policy.md are rollout/legacy-caller text copied from the Tools checker docs and won't age well here. One local test command also refers to another repository with no path or link.
